summary: Read-only: map what is NOT gated/tested across the 33 cells + Phase-2 + tooling + the new knobs — where a bug could hide undetected (the SG11 class was a coverage gap)

ranked_gaps.what_untested: The SG11/SG15 momentum-divergence gate — the test written SPECIFICALLY to catch the historic SG11 bug class (cos(grad,mu) vs canonical cos(grad,momentum)) — is NEVER collected by pytest. Only run_sg11_warmup_gate (tests/hw/test_l3tc_tail_gate.py:882) exercises it, and it is reachable ONLY via the CLI flag `--sg11-warmup` (main() at :1488-1499). The single decorated pytest entry test_l3tc_cell_gate (:1457-1473) runs run_cell_gate → the COLD step-1 path, which the file's own docstring (:884-887) admits is BLIND: at step 1 m=v=0 so cos(grad,mu)==cos(grad,momentum)==gate(0.5), the two formulations COINCIDE. SG15 is worse: run_sg11_warmup_gate hard-asserts opt=="supergrok11" (:904), so even the CLI warmup path cannot cover the 3 SG15 cells, which share the staged P2.45 mu/cosine-gate machinery (opt_stages_precompute.cuh) and are gated single-step only.
ranked_gaps.how_to_cover: Wrap run_sg11_warmup_gate in @pytest.mark.hw tests parametrized over the 3 supergrok11 cells (test_sg11_warmup_gate_<model>), asserting ok ∧ gate_div>1e-4 ∧ mom_norm≫0 — it already self-asserts non-vacuity, it just needs a pytest entry that skips cleanly off-GPU. Generalize the SG11-only assert at :904 into an SG15 analog (warm momentum, assert cos(grad,exp_avg) tracks the fp64 reference and the gate operand is exp_avg not mu) so all 6 SG-tier cells get a warm-momentum gate.

ranked_gaps.what_untested: Multi-step parity (the gate that catches step-1-blind machinery) exists ONLY for grokadamw and prodigy and ONLY on the decoder: test_multistep_parity.py hardcodes model="decoder" at :421 and :568, with no parametrization. Two independent blind spots: (a) the vit/mamba twins of grokadamw (grad-norm clip, inert when ‖g‖<1 at step 1) and prodigy (d-adaptation, frozen at d0 when r=0 at step 1) have NO multi-step gate — the single-step gate self-admits it is blind to both (test_l3tc_tail_gate.py:351-363, :376-394). (b) muon (persistent momentum buf=mu*buf+g compounding), looksam (every-k SAM cadence), sg11/sg15 (momentum-dependent gate + per-coord alpha clip), and sg2 (GRU/slow-EMA carry) have NO multi-step gate for ANY model — all five are single-step-only, yet the grokadamw/prodigy file itself states single-step is 'necessary but not sufficient'.
ranked_gaps.how_to_cover: Parametrize test_multistep_parity.py over model∈{decoder,vit,mamba} for grokadamw and prodigy (the _GrokAdamWRef/_ProdigyRef drivers are model-agnostic; only _build_cell(model) changes) with the non-vacuity asserts (clip fired by step 50; d grew off d0). Add new multi-step parity drivers for muon (assert momentum buffer + params track ref_muon_step over N steps), looksam (run >k steps so both a SAM and an intervening cached-direction step occur), sg11/sg15 (warm momentum, gate+apply over N steps), and sg2 (carry gru_state/slow/m/v forward; liveness assert gru_state moved off zero).

ranked_gaps.what_untested: The ViT B1 SG_TUNED_VIT_P1_SUBTILE_S<64 ON-path (the #1 perf lever, task #29) is NEVER compiled by any test or the autotuner. Default is 64 (model_stage_vit_tc.cuh:163-164); the entire ON-path — the m_real cross-CTA read-before-write row-guard and the sub-tile partition logic — is #if-erased at 6 guard sites (:386,:492,:516,:535,:831,:1110). Verified absent: the TC test builds with only -DSG_TUNED_GEMM_IMPL=1 and no -DSG_TUNED_VIT_P1_SUBTILE_S (test_vit_tc.py:682); the knob is not in compile.py's search space; not in _tuned_inject.py's MACROS table. So every build the gate, the autotuner, and CI ever see runs the OFF path; the new code is dead in all of them.
ranked_gaps.how_to_cover: Add a parametrized JIT gate in test_vit_tc.py / test_l3tc_tail_gate.py that compiles the ViT TC TU with -DSG_TUNED_VIT_P1_SUBTILE_S in {1,2,32} and runs the existing fp64 single-step + A/A/A parity vs the S=64 build (the regrouped fp32 sums must hold the documented ~1e-4 reorder band, and A/A/A must hold per S). Gate the knob BEFORE it can ship as a winner; add SUBTILE_S to the autotuner MACROS table only behind that gate.

ranked_gaps.what_untested: The autotune winner correctness hook documents PRODUCTION-scale validation that does not happen. _default_correctness_hook (compile.py:7213) — the IL=4-trap defense (task #28) every generated/synth/polyhedral winner must clear — docstrings 'PRODUCTION-scale (d=2048)' (:7220) and the inner comment claims 'the SAME cell gate at production scale' (:7271-7272), but the body calls _run_cell_gate(cell_key) (:7275) → run_cell_gate → _build_cell at the toy grokking scale (p=97, baked d=128/seq=4, test_l3tc_tail_gate.py:564). There is no d=2048 rebuild anywhere in the hook. This is the SG11 co-derivation shape: the validator's claimed scale and its actual scale disagree, so a winner that is fp64-correct at d=128 but breaks at d=2048 (occupancy spill changing results, a tile-count-dependent reduction) is accepted and published.
ranked_gaps.how_to_cover: Make the hook actually rebuild+gate at d=2048 (a scaled cell), OR fix the docstring/comment AND add a separate scaled correctness gate the winner must clear before publish. The d=2048 roofline-report scale and the correctness-gate scale must be reconciled in one place so they cannot drift again.

ranked_gaps.what_untested: The staged-precompute path (opt_stages_precompute.cuh — the PRODUCTION path #included by all 3 megakernels) is validated ONLY against hand-transcribed Python fp32 mirrors, never against the compiled device function. test_opt_stages.py:1-26 states 'the CUDA header is not compiled in this phase'; _prodigy_stage_mirror (:100), _sg11_gate_mirror_fp32 (:201), _muon_matmul_mirror (:429) are Python re-implementations checked vs the fp64 oracle. A bug present in the .cuh AND transcribed identically into the mirror (the exact SG11 co-wrong-oracle failure mode) is invisible. The historical 'mega_*_prodigy.cu actually ran AdamW' false-positive (opt_components.cuh:7-11) is this class. The muon mirror further only covers tiny shapes — NS up to 128x96 (test_opt_stages.py:402) and a 5x3 stride/transpose probe (:457) — while the real kernel orthogonalizes [512,128], [336,256] x_proj, and extreme-aspect dt_proj [4,8] (model_stage_mamba_tc.cuh:87-89, kMbMuonMaxRows=512), none of which the mirror runs.
ranked_gaps.how_to_cover: Add a GPU @pytest.mark.hw gate that JIT-compiles a thin harness exporting the ACTUAL opt_stages_precompute.cuh device functions (or asserts the in-megakernel staged result) and diffs them against the SAME fp64 oracles the CPU mirrors use, for prodigy/muon/sg11/sg15. Extend the muon shape parametrization to the real kernel shapes (512x512, 336x256, 384x128, 4x8) with per-shape NS tolerances. At minimum add an AST/checksum drift-guard binding the mirror formulas to the header.

ranked_gaps.what_untested: Every fp64+A/A/A gate runs at the toy grokking scale with compile-time-baked dims (decoder d=128/seq=4/vocab=99, vit d=128/seq=17, mamba d=128/seq=8; _build_cell p=97 at test_l3tc_tail_gate.py:564, _build at _sg2_l3tc_gate.py:46-57). No gate exercises the 1B+/d=2048 production scale of task #22. At d=128 each tensor fits in one tile / few CTAs; at scale the grad reduction becomes multi-CTA-per-tensor, prodigy's owner-sum tree spans many CTAs (the CPU mirror tops out at n_ctas=132, ~4k-element tensors, test_opt_stages.py:156), the global grad-norm clip reduction (P2.5) and muon's Frobenius reduction at rows=512 grow fp32 error, and FWD_STAGES>2 takes the dynamic-smem path. A multi-CTA reduction race, tile-boundary indexing bug, owner-sum slot overflow, or fixed-order fp32-accumulation error that only manifests when a tensor spans >1 CTA passes the entire suite; A/A/A at d=128 does not prove determinism across hundreds of CTAs.
ranked_gaps.how_to_cover: Add a scaled gate variant: a JIT-built TU with larger -DSG_*_D / -DSG_*_SEQ (or multi-layer) so at least one tensor spans many CTAs, then run the fp64 single-step + A/A/A gate and re-derive tolerances. Even one mid-scale point (d=512) covers the multi-CTA reduction class; reuse it as the scaled correctness gate for RG4.

ranked_gaps.what_untested: The only test that builds+runs the REAL 7B 3D-parallel (DP×TP×PP×ZeRO-3) fused step (test_3d_parallel_smoke) asserts ONLY thr>0.0 (test_3d_parallel.py:295) — a liveness check, not correctness — and _maybe_skip()s unless world_size>1 (:285-295). On CPU/CI only sizing/partition MATH runs (:240-273). Worse, the foundation has ZERO tests: _build_mesh / _coords_from_rank / _rank_from_coords (distributed.py:235-292) have no unit test (grep: no test references them, no mesh test file exists), and _init_groups (:379-436), all_reduce_ep + the EP axis (:546-555, expert_parallel field :99), _bucketize (:188), all_reduce_dp_grads ZeRO-0/1/2 (:557-592), and the reduce_scatter_grads older-torch fallback (:912-916) are exercised only inside the thr>0 harness or not at all. A wrong rank-to-group linearization, EP group misassignment, or fallback that returns an unreduced slice corrupts grads silently and is only observable under a real launch with a correctness assertion that doesn't exist.
ranked_gaps.how_to_cover: Add a CPU-only test_distributed_mesh.py: for (DP=4,TP=2,PP=2) assert _coords_from_rank∘_rank_from_coords is identity over all 16 ranks, dp/tp/pp groups are disjoint-within-dim and cover the world once, and Megatron TP-fastest holds; add an (DP=4,EP=2) EP-consecutive-pair check. Unit-test _bucketize (every element once, in order, size cap respected), all_reduce_dp_grads (== mean of per-rank grads via mock dist), and the reduce_scatter fallback (monkeypatch out reduce_scatter_tensor). Add a cross-gather correctness assertion to test_3d_parallel_smoke (all ranks bit-identical params ∧ params moved) and a world=2/4 subgroup-sentinel check after _init_groups. Execute task #21.

ranked_gaps.what_untested: The OptId→stage→apply-tail dispatch consistency across the C++ codegen and the Python dispatch is NOT asserted as a unit. test_verdict_partition_covers_all_eleven (test_opt_stages.py:489-502) checks only Python set literals (STAGED/NOTHING_NEEDED/MODEL_COUPLED/SKIP/TRIVIAL); it never reads the C++. The OptId enum (opt_components.cuh:53-56: Prodigy=5,NeuralGrok=6,Muon=7,SG11=8,SG15=9,SG2=10), optimizer_needs_precompute / the staged static_assert set, and dispatch.py's opt_id integers (routed by COMMENT only — 'routes opt_id=8/9' at dispatch.py:898/914) are bound by a hand-maintained 'KEEP IN LOCK-STEP with dispatch.cpp' contract (opt_components.cuh:332), with no automated cross-check. A future enum reorder, or sg15 given sg11's gate stage, passes the Python verdict test while a cell runs the wrong precompute — the literal 'mega_*_prodigy.cu actually ran AdamW' class (opt_components.cuh:10).
ranked_gaps.how_to_cover: Add a drift-guard test that parses the OptId enum + the staged set + optimizer_needs_precompute from the .cuh and asserts they match the Python partition AND dispatch.py's opt_id integers (modeled on the existing SG_TUNED MACROS drift guard). Also add a test that calls a launcher binding with an out-of-range opt_id (e.g. 99) and asserts the default: cudaErrorInvalidValue → LOUD throw (mega_mamba_real_adamw_tc_launcher.cu:262) is reachable and not dead-code-eliminated.

ranked_gaps.what_untested: The decoder cp.async ring is gated only at its single baked point. SG_TUNED_DEC_FWD_PIPE=1, SG_TUNED_DEC_FWD_STAGES=4 are baked (model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:186,189 — the STAGES>2 dynamic-smem path is the shipped default) and the TC test compiles only that point (-DSG_TUNED_GEMM_IMPL=1, no PIPE/STAGES override, test_decoder_tc.py:785). No test sweeps PIPE/STAGES; PIPE=0 (the designated byte-identical revert target) and PIPE=2 (the rejected tournament loser, kDecFwdPipeEngine, compiled-OUT by default at :255,:860) have no ON-path or revert-safety gate; the compile.py pipe_depth/gemm_stages dims are 'auto-pinned to in-source defaults' so the autotuner never compiles alternatives. The smem arena sizing and deeper-ring drain interact with the grad reduce. The coming EPI_R1 epilogue-ring lever does not yet exist in source, so its future ON-path has zero scaffolding.
ranked_gaps.how_to_cover: Add a knob-sweep gate that JIT-compiles the decoder TC TU across {PIPE=1/STAGES=4 (baked, must match the shipped .so), PIPE=0 (assert byte-identical to PIPE=1 within fp floor), PIPE=2, STAGES=2/3} and runs fp64 single-step + A/A/A for each. Stand up the same scaffold so EPI_R1's ON-path is gated the day it lands.

ranked_gaps.what_untested: LookSAM (and the SG11/SG15 SAM tier) are gated only on a SAM step. k=5 with _global_step starting at 0 means step 1 is a SAM step (test_l3tc_tail_gate.py:130-132,428), so the gate only ever exercises the SAM-ON branch (the 2nd in-kernel backward). The SAM-OFF branch — where the kernel must NOT run the 2nd backward and must reuse/decay the cached sam_dir in the blend g_adj=(1−α)g+α·sam_dir (looksam.h:6-7 'reused as a cached direction for intervening steps') — is never gated for apply correctness. Over a real run 4 of every 5 steps are SAM-off, so the DOMINANT looksam/SG11/SG15 code path is untested.
ranked_gaps.how_to_cover: Add a step-2..k gate (or a looksam multi-step parity) exercising a SAM-OFF step: run k=2 with one warm SAM step then a SAM-off step, asserting the kernel does NOT recompute sam_dir (extra slice unchanged within fp floor) and the apply blends the cached direction, vs an fp64 ref of the same. Folds naturally into the RG2 looksam multi-step driver.

ranked_gaps.what_untested: Prodigy's cross-CTA d-reduce uses the drain-then-barrier shape the header itself flags as the SG11-class hazard: opt_stages_precompute.cuh:453-468 documents that a full-queue drain followed by a separate apply drain SILENTLY NO-OPs (next_block returns t>=n_tasks) unless the counter is reset, and notes 'Prodigy DOES need a barrier because its d is a genuine cross-ALL-tensors reduction.' In the decoder this relies on B2 having reset g_next_task and P3's drain being the only post-B2.6 drain (fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:1202-1203). The CPU mirror asserts only owner-sum partition-INDEPENDENCE (test_opt_stages.py:163-180) — it cannot model the real queue-counter/barrier interaction — and the only device multistep prodigy test is decoder-only (test_multistep_parity.py:568). On vit/mamba (different tensor counts feed the cross-tensor sum) a barrier/reset interaction leaving the apply drain a no-op would skip the apply on some tensors with no test to catch it.
ranked_gaps.how_to_cover: Parametrize test_prodigy_multistep_parity over model∈{decoder,vit,mamba} (RG2), and add an assertion that EVERY tensor was actually updated by P3 after the d-reduce drain (params changed) at high n_ctas, so a silent apply-drain no-op fails loudly.

ranked_gaps.what_untested: Several Phase-2 gates are model-narrowed in ways that leave per-model layout drift uncovered. ZeRO-3 checkpoint round-trip is decoder-only and elementwise-only (test_zero3_roundtrip.py:54 _CELLS=[adamw,grokfast], model hardcoded decoder :72) — vit/mamba ZeRO-3 gather/scatter is ungated (sharded-opt covers vit/mamba but only the B2 seam, not the full round-trip). CUDA-graph capture hard-asserts model=="decoder" (test_step_graph_capture.py:136), so vit/mamba persistent-buffer addressing under replay is ungated. PP=2 loopback is decoder-only (test_pp2_loopback_determinism.py:253; pipeline.py raises for non-decoder). DP=2 loopback omits mamba entirely (_DP2_CELLS = decoder×{adamw,lion,grokfast}+vit×adamw, :429-431) and the world=2 distributed-step path hardcodes --opt adamw (test_distributed_step.py:272), so lion's sharded_apply scalar wiring is never validated under a real collective. Mamba's distinct flat layout (28 tensors, SSM conv weight) could put a shard boundary inside a model-specific tensor that decoder-only gates never expose.
ranked_gaps.how_to_cover: Parametrize ZeRO-3 round-trip and DP=2 loopback over {decoder,vit,mamba} (the _build_cell(model) infra already exists in test_sharded_optimizer.py); extend run_chain_graph_capture to vit/mamba input packing; parametrize the world=2 distributed-step over {adamw,lion,grokfast} via separate master_ports; add ViT/Mamba PP layout + a pp2 ownership cross-check when PP support lands.

ranked_gaps.what_untested: The grad-norm clip cold-start path for neuralgrok is exercised only when the clip FIRES, but GATE_SEED defaults to 42 (clip inert, norm<grad_clip; test_l3tc_tail_gate.py:222-223,551) and is NEVER parametrized in any test — only settable via an env var (grep: no parametrize/monkeypatch of GATE_SEED anywhere). The firing seed (e.g. 7) and the unclipped-EMA-seed cold-start interaction are never auto-run, and neuralgrok has NO multistep test (unlike grokadamw, whose clip-fire analog bug was found via its multistep test). So neuralgrok's clip-coefficient application ships validated only in the clip-inert regime.
ranked_gaps.how_to_cover: Parametrize the neuralgrok cell gate over GATE_SEED including a seed where ‖g‖2>grad_clip (clip fires at step 1), asserting state parity in the firing regime; and/or add a neuralgrok multistep parity test that crosses the clip threshold like the grokadamw one.

ranked_gaps.what_untested: mamba×supergrok2 is documented as possibly 'landing dormant' if A/A/A re-trips — the SAM double-forward + segmented sort re-exercise the shared mamba forward race (test_l3tc_tail_gate.py:530-538). The dedicated launcher mega_mamba_sg2_tc DOES exist (mega_mamba_real_adamw_tc_launcher.cu:282 — so this is NOT a dead-dispatch bug), but no test distinguishes a LIVE landing from a dormant one: the SG2 A/A/A runs only 3× from the same init (_sg2_l3tc_gate.py:218,237), too few to catch flaky nondeterminism, and a dormant landing (kernel present, A/A/A intermittently failing) is not asserted separately. The same shared-forward re-entry risk applies to the other mamba SAM-tier cells (looksam/SG11/SG15/mamba).
ranked_gaps.how_to_cover: Run the mamba SAM-tier A/A/A (SG2, looksam, SG11, SG15) with ≥10 repeats and/or across multiple builds, and add an explicit LIVE assertion (A/A/A passes N×) so a dormant/flaky landing fails loudly rather than being a documented maybe.

ranked_gaps.what_untested: Two future-facing distributed paths have only compile-time coverage. (1) ZeRO stages 0/1/2 have no functional gate: test_parallel_instantiation.py compiles ParConfig<...,Z2> with nvcc -c to /dev/null (no run, :74-77) and the sharded-opt gate exercises only ZeRO-3 semantics; all_reduce_dp_grads (the ZeRO-0/1/2 grad reduce) is never called in any test, so a ZeRO-2 run silently taking the ZeRO-3 gather path or no-opping is undetected. (2) The per-tensor optimizers (muon/SG11/SG15/SG2) are loudly rejected by fused_train_step_distributed (distributed_step.py:91-96) and excluded from every distributed gate — so when the tensor-granular shard path is wired (design §2.3) there is no pre-existing correctness baseline for muon's NS / SG11's gate-mu stages under sharding.
ranked_gaps.how_to_cover: Add a torchrun world=2 ZeRO-2 test asserting each rank applies the optimizer only to its owned shard, all_reduce_dp_grads actually averages (not a no-op), and params converge to a single-GPU ZeRO-0 reference within parity tol. Add a CPU-level tensor-granular-plan test that runs the muon plan through a virtual world=2 gather/release loop with an fp64 muon step and asserts the reassembled shards equal a single-GPU fp64 muon step — catching the shard boundary + gather plumbing before the GPU binding lands.

ranked_gaps.what_untested: Two SG2-specific checks are toothless. (1) The tie-probe (keystone for sort top-risk #1) does NOT validate the in-kernel segmented sort against |grad| ties: by its own admission it cannot read the kernel's perm (_sg2_l3tc_gate.py:290-302), so it feeds the tied grad to the ORACLE's own _strategy_a_perm builder and asserts THAT is a total order + deterministic (:303-315) — a property of the test helper, not the kernel. B1 uses tie-free continuous grads (perm unique regardless of tie policy) and A/A/A only proves the kernel is deterministic, not that it matches the (|g|,idx) index-tie-break — so an unstable in-kernel comparator on equal |grad| passes (the SG11 co-wrong-oracle shape). (2) The N>64 CSA fidelity divergence is REPORTED, never asserted (:18-20,:320-333): every real tensor has numel≫64 so the kernel always runs the low-rank indexer, and the fp64 oracle_step deliberately uses the SAME low-rank indexer (:323), so a regression that enlarges the divergence (unstable indexer, wrong /sqrt scaling) is absorbed into a report line with no threshold.
ranked_gaps.how_to_cover: For the tie-probe: construct an input that FORCES the kernel down a tied-|grad| path observably (recover the per-element update ordering through the mu/state the kernel produces) and assert it matches the (|g|,idx) order and NOT a deliberately-wrong tie order. For N>64: convert the report to a bounded check — assert the low-rank-vs-bilevel divergence on the largest tensor stays within a documented band so a regression that enlarges it fails, keeping it informational that the gap exists by design.

synth.notes:
VERIFIED READ-ONLY against /workspace/SuperGrok1.5. The two input gap-lists overlap heavily; I deduplicated into 16 ranked gaps (e.g. G1≈G3≈GAP-03 → RG1; G4≈G6≈GAP-04 → RG3; G7/G1(list2)/GAP-06 → RG5; G5/GAP-08 → RG4; the Phase-2 mesh/EP/thr-only cluster → RG7). Ranking is risk_if_buggy × likelihood-of-hiding-a-bug.

KEY CORRECTION (cite before acting): GAP-11 (mamba×sg2 'no launcher, dead registration') is REFUTED — the dedicated launcher mega_mamba_sg2_tc exists (mega_mamba_real_adamw_tc_launcher.cu:282) and the default: throw returns cudaErrorInvalidValue (:262). The real mamba×SG2 risk is the documented dormant-landing / flaky A/A/A (test_l3tc_tail_gate.py:533-534), folded into RG14. Everything else verified at the cited lines.

SPOT-CHECKS that confirmed the worst items: only test_l3tc_cell_gate carries @pytest.mark.hw in the tail gate (one decorator block at :1457-1459); run_sg11_warmup_gate is CLI-only (:1488) and hard-asserts supergrok11 (:904) so SG15 has no warm path at all. _default_correctness_hook body calls _run_cell_gate→_build_cell(p=97) (:7275) despite the 'production scale (d=2048)' docstring (:7220) and inner comment (:7271). SG_TUNED_VIT_P1_SUBTILE_S is absent from compile.py, _tuned_inject.py, and both TC test files (grep returned nothing). GATE_SEED is never parametrized (default 42, clip-inert). PIPE/STAGES baked at 1/4. test_3d_parallel_smoke asserts only thr>0.0 and _maybe_skips off-multi-GPU. _build_mesh/_init_groups/all_reduce_ep/_bucketize have zero test references.

THE SYSTEMIC GAP (the SG11 bug's shape, recurring): the gate suite is structurally blind along four axes simultaneously — (1) SINGLE-STEP-ONLY from zero-init state (m=v=0, gru_state=0, d=d0, clip inert, first SAM step), so every momentum/EMA/clip/d-adaptation/cached-SAM mechanism is exercised in the one regime where the buggy and correct formulations coincide; (2) TINY-SCALE-ONLY with compile-time-baked dims (p=97, d=128), so every multi-CTA reduction, owner-sum tree, and dynamic-smem path is single-CTA-degenerate; (3) the correctness anchor is a HAND-TRANSCRIBED MIRROR (opt_stages CPU fp32 mirrors) or an ORACLE THAT CO-DERIVES the kernel's own choice (SG2 tie-probe validates the oracle's perm builder; N>64 oracle uses the same low-rank indexer; the autotune hook claims d=2048 but co-runs the tiny gate), so a co-wrong oracle/mirror hides the bug; (4) ON-PATHS for new knobs and the warm/firing/SAM-off branches are NEVER COMPILED OR REACHED (SUBTILE_S<64, PIPE=0/2, --sg11-warmup, GATE_SEED=7, step%k≠0). The SG11 root cause was (1)+(3) together. Close the CLASS, not the instances, with five standing rules: (a) every gated mechanism must have a regime where the canonical and a deliberately-wrong formulation DIVERGE (warm momentum, fired clip, adapted d, multi-step, SAM-off) — single-step is necessary-not-sufficient by policy; (b) every -D knob's ON-path must be JIT-compiled-and-gated before it can ship/win (a 'no ungated ON-path' merge gate); (c) at least one multi-CTA / scaled point must clear the same fp64+A/A/A gate, and the autotune correctness hook must run at the SAME scale its docstring claims; (d) device-vs-fp64 must be the comparison of record for the staged path (or an AST/checksum drift-guard binds the mirror to the header); (e) cross-language contracts (OptId↔dispatch.py, Python verdict sets↔C++ staged set) need an automated drift-guard, not a 'KEEP IN LOCK-STEP' comment. Phase-2: promote the single-GPU loopback determinism + cross-rank-identity + correctness-parity checks (and the CPU mesh/EP/bucketize units) into the default gate rather than runbook-only, and add a correctness assertion (cross-rank bit-identity ∧ params-moved) to the 3D smoke beyond thr>0.
